title: New Orleans musicians Rinker met in Chicago
summary: Rinker lists the New Orleans players he knew, from Rag Baby Stevens and Larry Shields to the Brunies brothers, Paul Mares, Bouchon, Natty Dominique and the Bobcats men, and recalls evening trumpet duets by phone with Mares.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: During that time I played with many musicians from New Orleans. I believe the first one I met was Rag Baby Stevens, drummer. That was when I was playing out on Milwaukee Avenue about the first job I ever played. A place called the House of Niles. I think I met Larry Shields there also. Shortly after that I played at a place on West Madison Street owned by Tommy Thomas in which Ray Bozeman was the saxophone clarinet player and he was a very excellent one. And shortly after that I met the Bruny's boys Merritt, Henry, and George and later Paul Merez of course. I remembered them for many years and became quite friendly with Paul Merez later on. After that I played with Lester Bouchon and his friend Westerfield. We called him Eagle. I can't remember his first name. They were both saxophone players, excellent ones. I knew Steve Brown. I played with him at the Midway Gardens. Natty Dominick, a personal friend of mine at Burt Kelly Stables. He is to this day. He taught me much about the trumpet. And of course I know the boys that played with the uh with the Pollack and the uh and the Bobcat bands. Benny Pollack and later with the Bobcats there was uh Irving Pizzola. I knew him quite well. Played with him several times. And uh Matty Matlock, Nappy Lamar, Eddie Miller, and Ray Badouf whom I knew well. Let's see who else from New Orleans. Oh there were so many. Many of the colored musicians from New Orleans I knew. How many of them came from there and how many didn't I don't I really know. Let's see. I got to know Paul quite well when he was running his Shrimp de Jong place on uh Bryn Mawr and I was living close to there. He used to pick up his telephone and call me and then he would play the trumpet to me and I would play the trumpet back to him. And we used to pass the evenings away that way occasionally. That was not too long before he passed away. I don't know John if I can remember anybody else in New Orleans or not. So many fellas came from there that I didn't really know.
